## What I found

The StatefulSet `app` declared `spec.serviceName: app` with `selector: app=app` and `containerPort: 80` (named `http`), and its 2 Pods were Running/Ready — but `kubectl get svc` showed only `service/kubernetes`, so no governing headless Service existed and no per-Pod DNS records could be created.

## Change made

Created one new object (nothing existing was modified or deleted):

```
service/app  ClusterIP  None  80/TCP  selector=app=app  namespace=default
```

`clusterIP: None`, `selector: app=app`, `port: 80` → `targetPort: 80`.

## Verification (fresh observations after the change)

**Service spec** — `clusterIP=None`, `type=ClusterIP`, `selector={"app":"app"}`, `port=80` ✔

**Endpoints/EndpointSlice** — `endpoints/app` → `10.244.0.4:80,10.244.0.6:80`; EndpointSlice `app-kl6vr` → `10.244.0.6,10.244.0.4` ✔

**Per-Pod stable DNS, resolved from inside `app-0`** — each name maps to the correct Pod IP:

| Name | Resolved |
|---|---|
| `app-0.app.default.svc.cluster.local` | `10.244.0.4` (= app-0) |
| `app-1.app.default.svc.cluster.local` | `10.244.0.6` (= app-1) |
| `app` (headless, all endpoints) | `10.244.0.4`, `10.244.0.6` |

**Requests through the Service succeed** on port 80 — `curl` returned `http_code=200` via `app-0.app...` (10.244.0.4:80), via `app-1.app...` (10.244.0.6:80), and via `http://app/` (10.244.0.4:80).

**Controller still healthy** — requested=2, ready=2, updated=2, available=2; `serviceName=app` now matches the existing Service.

The originally reported symptom — Pods having no stable per-Pod DNS names — is gone: all three names resolve to the intended Pod IPs and serve HTTP 200.
